items.title: Composite trapezoidal rule
items.statement: For a<b, an integer N>=1, mesh width h=(b-a)/N, and a real-valued f on [a,b], define T_N(f)=h[ f(a)/2 + sum_{j=1}^{N-1} f(a+jh) + f(b)/2 ].
items.strategy: Define the deterministic equal-mesh quadrature value and state its input domain without asserting an error estimate.

references.title: Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6.1–§5.6.4
references.locator: Equations (5.6.1)–(5.6.4), composite trapezoid weights and formula; complete online chapter inspected.

references.title: Endre Süli, Numerical Computation, course notes
references.locator: §2.2, composite trapezium rule, equation (20), PDF pp. 15–16.

items.title: Gaussian integral for a positive-definite quadratic form
items.statement: Assuming Countable Choice, for every d>=1 and every real symmetric positive-definite H in M_d(R), the Lebesgue integral over R^d of exp(-u^T H u/2) equals (2 pi)^(d/2)/sqrt(det H).
items.strategy: Use the real spectral theorem to identify the positive eigenvalue branch, Cholesky factorization for an invertible linear change of variables, Tonelli for the product Gaussian, and the one-dimensional Gaussian integral.

references.title: Laplace method for integrals, PHYS 2400, University of Connecticut
references.locator: Complete 7-page PDF inspected, especially the Gaussian reductions on pp. 2–6; the exact multivariate integral is proved locally.

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §2.3(iii), Laplace's Method
references.locator: Equations (2.3.13)–(2.3.18) and conditions (a)–(c); one-dimensional endpoint formulation, used as asymptotic context only.

references.title: Francis Bach, Approximating Integrals with Laplace's Method
references.locator: The multidimensional Hessian and Jacobian derivation in the opening Laplace approximation argument; the local proof supplies domination and tails.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is used by the Lebesgue and box-measure, Borel-to-Lebesgue, Riemann–Lebesgue equality, product-completion, and C^1 change-of-variables suppliers. No full Axiom of Choice is used.

items.title: Pointwise linear interpolation error from a second-derivative bound
items.statement:
Let $a<b$ and let $f$ be $C^2$ on an open interval containing $[a,b]$. Put
$M:=\sup_{t\in[a,b]}|f''(t)|$, which is finite, and let $L$ be the unique affine
function with $L(a)=f(a)$ and $L(b)=f(b)$. Then for every $x\in[a,b]$,
$$|f(x)-L(x)|\le \frac{M}{2}(x-a)(b-x).$$
items.strategy: Apply Rolle's theorem twice to a correction that vanishes at both endpoints and at the chosen interior point, obtaining the exact second-order interpolation remainder.

references.title: Endre Süli, Numerical Computation, course notes
references.locator: §1.1, Theorem 1 (Cauchy interpolation remainder), equations (5)–(6), specialized to degree-one interpolation.

items.title: Laplace asymptotic under a unique nondegenerate interior maximum
items.statement: For I_n=int_K a(theta) exp(n h(theta)) dtheta on a compact measurable K subset R^d of positive Lebesgue measure, assume a>=0 is measurable and integrable, is continuous at the unique interior maximizer theta-hat, and a(theta-hat)>0; h is continuous on K and C^3 near theta-hat; H=-D^2 h(theta-hat) is symmetric positive definite; h has a local quadratic upper bound at theta-hat and a strict global gap away from a neighborhood. Then I_n is asymptotic to a(theta-hat) exp(n h(theta-hat)) (2 pi/n)^(d/2)/sqrt(det H).
items.strategy: Prove the interior gradient vanishes, use second-order Taylor expansion and a bounded third-order remainder after u=sqrt(n)(theta-theta-hat), apply dominated convergence under the local quadratic bound, and show the integrable off-mode contribution is exponentially small using the compact gap.

references.title: Laplace method for integrals, PHYS 2400, University of Connecticut
references.locator: Complete 7-page PDF inspected, pp. 1–7; heuristic derivations and endpoint/nonquadratic examples are treated as context, not proof.

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §2.3(iii), Laplace's Method
references.locator: Equations (2.3.13)–(2.3.18) and conditions (a)–(c); the local theorem has its own hypotheses and complete proof.

references.title: Francis Bach, Approximating Integrals with Laplace's Method
references.locator: Opening compact-domain multidimensional formula and its Hessian/Jacobian derivation; the local proof supplies the missing domination and off-mode bound.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from lem-positive-definite-gaussian-integral through the cited C^1 Lebesgue change-of-variables theorem; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

items.title: Second-derivative error bound for the composite trapezoidal rule
items.statement: For f in C^2[a,b], N>=1, h=(b-a)/N, and T_N as defined, |int_a^b f-T_N| <= (b-a) h^2 ||f''||_infinity/12.
items.strategy: On each mesh cell compare f with its endpoint linear interpolant, integrate the exact pointwise interpolation bound, sum by additivity, and evaluate the elementary quadratic integral.

references.title: Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6.1–§5.6.4
references.locator: Equations (5.6.1)–(5.6.4), composite formula, and the second-order accuracy discussion; complete online chapter inspected.

references.title: Endre Süli, Numerical Computation, course notes
references.locator: §2.1, Theorem 3 and equation (14) for one panel; §2.2, equations (20)–(21) for the composite trapezium error, PDF pp. 12–16.

title: Laplace approximation and deterministic quadrature — Examples

items.title: An exact Gaussian Laplace integral on the noncompact line
items.statement: For h(theta)=c-(theta-mu)^2/2 on R and amplitude one, the integral of exp(n h(theta)) is exactly exp(nc) sqrt(2 pi/n), agreeing with its quadratic-mode approximation; the compact theorem is not invoked.
items.strategy: Evaluate by a positive affine change of variable in the one-dimensional Gaussian integral and compute the unique maximizer and Hessian directly.

references.title: Laplace method for integrals, PHYS 2400, University of Connecticut
references.locator: Complete 7-page PDF inspected, especially the Gaussian reductions on pp. 2 and 5–6; the exact evaluation is supplied locally.

items.title: A boundary mode has a different concentration rate
items.statement: The interior Gaussian formula remains valid at a unique boundary maximizer whenever the second derivative there is negative.
items.strategy: Use h(x)=-x-x^2 on [0,1]: the endpoint is the unique maximum, the second derivative is -2, but a direct upper bound makes the integral negligible relative to n^(-1/2).

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §2.3(iii), Laplace's Method
references.locator: Equation (2.3.15) and conditions (a)–(c), which explicitly treat an endpoint minimum in the one-dimensional formulation.

references.title: Laplace method for integrals, PHYS 2400, University of Connecticut
references.locator: Complete 7-page PDF inspected, pp. 2–3, for a boundary-dominated example with a nonquadratic endpoint phase; the counterexample is proved locally.

items.title: A singular interior mode need not have Gaussian scaling
items.statement: A unique interior maximum of a smooth phase always gives an integral of order exp(n h-hat)/sqrt(n), even when the Hessian is singular.
items.strategy: For h(x)=-x^4 on [-1,1], integrate only over a shrinking interval of width 2/m when n=m^4; there the integrand is at least e^(-1), so the integral is much larger than n^(-1/2).

references.title: Laplace method for integrals, PHYS 2400, University of Connecticut
references.locator: Complete 7-page PDF inspected, pp. 2–5, including a nonquadratic phase example; the interior singular-mode witness is proved locally.

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §2.3(iii), Laplace's Method
references.locator: Equations (2.3.14)–(2.3.18): the local power and amplitude orders determine the scale; the witness is proved locally.

items.title: Two equal modes contribute two Gaussian terms
items.statement: When two distinct nondegenerate interior maxima have equal height, the leading asymptotic term is the contribution from only one of the two modes.
items.strategy: For h(x)=-(x^2-1)^2 on [-2,2], apply the proved theorem separately on [-2,0] and [0,2], verify its hypotheses on each half, and add the two equal contributions.

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §2.3(iii), Laplace's Method
references.locator: Section §2.3(iii), equations (2.3.13)–(2.3.18), for localization at dominant modes; this two-mode calculation is proved locally.

references.title: Francis Bach, Approximating Integrals with Laplace's Method
references.locator: Opening discussion of a strict global minimizer and localization near the mode; the equal-mode sum is proved locally.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the Laplace theorem and used in the Lebesgue/Riemann integral comparison; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

items.title: The one-panel trapezoidal bound is attained by x squared
items.statement: For f(x)=x^2 on [0,1] with N=1, the one-panel trapezoidal error equals the stated second-derivative bound, h^2||f''||_infinity/12=1/6.
items.strategy: Compute the endpoint trapezoid, exact integral, and second-derivative supremum directly.

references.title: Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6.1–§5.6.4
references.locator: Equations (5.6.1)–(5.6.4) and the second-order accuracy discussion; complete online chapter inspected.
